# linearctl relation

<!-- Generated by scripts/skill-docs.py from --help; do not edit. -->

## linearctl relation create

```
Relate two issues. A relation that already exists is changed: false.
--id is a UUID you choose for the relation, so a rerun can never relate the two
twice: Linear refuses an id that is taken, and the result is then the existing
relation with changed: false. --dry-run without --id generates one and prints
it as id; pass it to --yes.
TYPE is one of:
  blocks      ISSUE blocks OTHER
  blocked-by  OTHER blocks ISSUE
  duplicate   ISSUE is a duplicate of OTHER
  related     ISSUE and OTHER are related (either direction)
  similar     ISSUE and OTHER are similar (either direction)
Changes things: pass --dry-run to preview, --yes to apply.

Usage:
  linearctl relation create ISSUE TYPE OTHER [flags]

Examples:
  linearctl relation create ENG-12 blocks ENG-15 --dry-run
  linearctl relation create ENG-12 duplicate ENG-9 --yes --json

Flags:
      --dry-run   show what would change; change nothing
  -h, --help      help for create
      --id UUID   the new relation's UUID; a rerun with it cannot create a second
      --yes       apply the change
```

## linearctl relation delete

```
Remove a relation between two issues. One that is not there is changed: false.
Without TYPE, removes every relation between the two, in either direction,
and lists each in relations.
TYPE is one of:
  blocks      ISSUE blocks OTHER
  blocked-by  OTHER blocks ISSUE
  duplicate   ISSUE is a duplicate of OTHER
  related     ISSUE and OTHER are related (either direction)
  similar     ISSUE and OTHER are similar (either direction)
Changes things: pass --dry-run to preview, --yes to apply.

Usage:
  linearctl relation delete ISSUE [TYPE] OTHER [flags]

Examples:
  linearctl relation delete ENG-12 blocks ENG-15 --dry-run
  linearctl relation delete ENG-12 duplicate ENG-9 --yes --json
  linearctl relation delete ENG-12 ENG-15 --dry-run --json

Flags:
      --dry-run   show what would change; change nothing
  -h, --help      help for delete
      --yes       apply the change
```
